newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent rallies on Iraq fears, funds, ends up 31c.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent rallies on Iraq fears, funds, ends up 31c.

text.p: IPE Brent futures rallied strongly on Friday to last trade at $18.16, up 31 cents, buoyed by prompt tightness in physical markets inspired by worries over Iraq exports and by fund buying, brokers said.

The August benchmark Brent blend contract climbed as high as $18.24 in the mid-afternoon before falling back. The New York Mercantile Exchange's front-month crude contract also rode higher, finishing at $19.45, up 36 cents on the day.
"We've got a slightly stronger market all over. There has been some fund buying as people roll over positons but basically crude has just wanted to lift," said one broker.
Traders said financial funds have been short for some time and may have been looking to cover before resuming bearish positions early next month.
IPE numbers were also boosted by heavy physical crude buying as traders covered July requirements early out of fear delays in the shipment of Iraqi barrels would leave the month tight.
Differentials on the wet market all firmed and demand was good, although benchmark Brent blend cargo was little talked.
Friday's gains were said to be largely technical and flew in the face of market scepticism OPEC's Vienna deal to freeze quotas would limit over-supply on world oil markets.

Quota cheaters within the 11-nation cartel produce about two million barrels per day above the supposed 25.03 million bpd and ignore pleas for restraint. The Vienna meeting was seen as doing little to improve compliance.
Fundamentals were expected to reassert themselves, with the resumption of Iraqi exports next month and excess OPEC crude likely to weigh on the market, traders said.
Earlier IPE gas oii closed stronger, up $2 on the day at $163.75, with a widening crack spread seen attracting buyers.
Dealers were unclear on Brent's direction next week, with failure to breach $18.32 and a recent high of $18.45 potentially
presaging downside when business restarts on Monday.
